| [CLAIM-395](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-395.md) | Under Montévil and Mossio's definition of closure, a closed set of constraints has at least two members, and if each constraint is produced at the time scale of a constraint in the set that generates it and not at the scale at which it is itself conserved, the set includes at least one slow and one fast dependence, so a system with a single constraint of its own cannot realise closure |  | Active |

| [CLAIM-400](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-400.md) v2 | In the meaning–authority model linearized at symmetry, a third, maintained legibility state that authority moves (ε) and that moves interpretation (ν) or endorsement (μ), with persistence λ < 1 and nonnegative couplings, destabilizes the symmetric state exactly when the two-variable condition holds with β + νε/(1 − λ) in place of β and δ + με/(1 − λ) in place of δ: at the threshold the regime is indistinguishable from stronger two-variable couplings, and the slower it is the more it adds, while away from the threshold it adds a mode that no two-variable model has, so a lean in the regime can outlast the advantages it was built from | [QUESTION-253](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-253.md) asked whether authority's effect on what becomes legible as evidence is a third channel with its own instability condition, or [CLAIM-340](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-340.md)'s κ′ renamed. Both, in different respects. With a maintained legibility state r, det(I − J₃) = (1 − λ)[(1 − α)(1 − δ) − βγ] − ε[νγ + μ(1 − α)], which is (1 − λ) times [CLAIM-330](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-330.md)'s expression with β_eff = β + νε/(1 − λ) and δ_eff = δ + με/(1 − λ). | [CLAIM-401](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-401.md) | The conditions an effective description is commonly asked to meet are not of one kind: predictive sufficiency and approximation fidelity are adequacy relative to a declared target, metric and horizon; tractability restricts the operations under which adequacy is assessed; dynamical independence and memory closure are relations of the representation to the system, memory relative to a chosen projection; so a matrix over them as independent binary axes conflates kinds | A4 and A5 of the exchange of 2026-10-20, on the owner's U4 ("it sounds like considering it from this angle has potentially already altered our characterization of those 'virtues'"). | [CLAIM-408](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-408.md) v3 | In ḋ = (α − κ)d − βd³, with d the difference between two parties' shares of authority, α their self-reinforcement and κ a constraint that bears on both alike, the equal allocation is the only equilibrium and is stable for κ > α, and for κ < α it is unstable and the unequal allocations ±√((α − κ)/β) are stable: a constraint that favours neither party can, by weakening, destabilize the equal allocation and make persistent unequal allocations stable, of any size near the threshold (\|d*\| → 0 as κ → α), without determining which party gains the larger share, and in this model restoring κ > α restores the equal allocation | A19 of the exchange of 2026-10-20, on the owner's U19: does the account "capture 'deregulation' as a disguised effort to induce organizational symmetry breaking?" A19's model is a supercritical pitchfork, [CASE-112](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-112.md)'s normal form with no tilt and μ = α − κ. The stability analysis is checked here, algebraically and numerically. The claim is about the model. It says nothing about any reform, or about anyone's intent, and it does not show that a tipped allocation outlasts the constraint's return: in this model it does not. | Active |
| [CLAIM-409](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-409.md) v2 | For one state law, one intervention distribution and one outcome, a deficiency of sufficiency cannot increase under refinement: if T₁ = g∘T₂ then Γ(T₂) ≤ Γ(T₁); informational closure, by contrast, is monotone in neither direction, since in the three-bit chain of Rosas et al. (2024) A is closed, its refinement (A, B) is not and the full state refining that is closed again, while A⊕B, a coarsening of (A, B), is not closed either; closure fails to be monotone because refining a description changes the future it must predict as well as the evidence, so Blackwell dominance, which every deterministic refinement has over its coarsening, does not order closure | Two readers' drafts of one point, from A6, A7, A16 and A17 of the exchange of 2026-10-20. A16 §5 and A17's Proposition 2: a fixed-target deficiency is refinement-monotone; "Adding information cannot hurt exact sufficiency for an unchanged question, but changing what the description is expected to explain can expose new dependencies." A6 §6 and A7's Proposition 3: "Increasing the information retained by a representation can destroy a desirable dynamical property", and "There is no general data-processing inequality ordering these quantities, because both the predicted variable and the conditioning information change." This claim joins them, and corrects A7's slogan "When More Information Reveals Less Autonomy": closure is not reversed by refinement, it is unordered by it. Checked exactly on 2026-10-21. | Active |
